abstract: Phosphate (Pi) and magnesium (Mg2+) are essential macronutrients that function together in numerous cellular processes. In natural soils, however, Pi scarcity is a far more pervasive constraint on plant productivity than Mg2+ limitation. How plants coordinate the allocation of these two nutrients under such imbalanced conditions remains largely unknown. Here, we uncover a nutrient-prioritization mechanism that allocates Mg2+ according to Pi availability in Arabidopsis thaliana. Elevated Pi supply alleviates Mg2+ deficiency, whereas Pi starvation renders Mg2+ physiologically ineffective for sustaining shoot growth, demonstrating that Pi is prioritized over Mg2+ in growth regulation. Mechanistically, local root Pi status controls the Pi-responsive transcription factors PHR1 and PHL1, which directly repress MGR4, the major transporter responsible for xylem Mg2+ loading. Under low Pi supply, activated PHR1/PHL1 restrict MGR4-dependent Mg2+ transport, preventing futile Mg2+ accumulation in Pi-starved shoots with arrested growth. As Pi availability increases, this repression of MGR4 is relieved, enhancing xylem Mg2+ loading and enabling Mg2+ to cooperate with Pi in sustaining shoot growth even under Mg2+-limiting conditions. Together, our findings identify local root Pi sensing as a nutritional rheostat that dynamically matches systemic Mg2+ allocation to Pi availability, thereby prioritizing Pi-dependent growth and maintaining shoot Pi-Mg2+ homeostasis under widespread Pi-limiting conditions.

summary: In Arabidopsis, root phosphate sensing via PHR1/PHL1 represses MGR4, controlling xylem Mg2+ loading so shoot Mg2+ allocation tracks phosphate availability.
title: Phosphate Availability Controls Shoot Magnesium Allocation through Local Root Phosphate Sensing in Arabidopsis.
